question: A doctor loses both inner-ear balance organs to an antibiotic. What troubles him most in daylight?
options: The world jiggling as he walks
answer: The world jiggling as he walks. Without the reflex that turns the eyes against each head movement, every footstep shakes the image. A physician who lost both organs to streptomycin wrote in 1952 that he could read in bed only with his head held still between the bars of the bedstead.
move: A failure spread evenly is harder to feel than a lopsided one.
ask: What slow change in my life am I missing because nothing about it feels sudden?
trap: Equating a lost balance organ with spinning dizziness.
source: J.C., New England Journal of Medicine, 1952
reference: J.C., Living without a balancing mechanism, New England Journal of Medicine, 1952
